title: Multimodal token routing lab
description: Trace grouped text, vision, layout, and joint tokens into a shared expert pool.

experts.label: Shared generalist
experts.role: Common transformation applied when the routing contract includes a shared path.

experts.label: Language patterns
experts.role: Observed specialization for instructions, syntax, and conversational context.

experts.label: Visual objects
experts.role: Observed specialization for shape, texture, and object evidence.

experts.label: Spatial layout
experts.role: Observed specialization for regions, tables, and document geometry.

experts.label: Cross-modal links
experts.role: Observed specialization for references that join words to visual evidence.

policies.label: Unified top-1
policies.detail: Each token group uses its highest-scoring routed expert.
policies.consequence: One dispatch per token keeps active work low, but a dominant visual group can create a hot expert.

policies.label: Shared plus top-1
policies.detail: Every token uses the shared expert and one routed specialist.
policies.consequence: Common capacity is always available, but dispatch work roughly doubles and the shared expert becomes a universal dependency.

policies.label: Modality-aware balance
policies.detail: Grouped tokens split between their first and second suitable experts to avoid one-modality collapse.
policies.consequence: Load spreads across suitable experts while retaining one routed assignment per token; quality still requires task evidence.

workloads.label: Visual question answering
workloads.brief: A short question asks about objects and their spatial relationship in one detailed image.

workloads.label: Scanned invoice extraction
workloads.brief: Layout and OCR evidence dominate a document request with a small instruction prompt.

workloads.label: Text-only chat turn
workloads.brief: No visual evidence is present, so a multimodal model should not manufacture visual specialization work.
